summary: Backend-only verification of UPDATE 1 (Vendor Shop scoping + publish gating). Wrote pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_vendor_publish_gating.py (9 tests, 4 test classes) covering all requested scenarios. ALL 9 TESTS PASS (100%). Verified: (1) POST /api/vendor/me/products force-sets is_published=False even when payload sends is_published=true; (2) POST without is_published also defaults to False; (3) GET /api/vendor/me/products returns vendor's own unpublished products; (4) GET /api/products (public) hides unpublished products; (5) PATCH /api/admin/products/{id} still toggles is_published (no regression); (6) after admin publishes, PATCH /api/vendor/me/products/{id} with is_published=false silently drops the field (product stays published) while other fields (description) update; (7) vendor PATCH with only is_published returns 400 'No fields provided' because the update dict is empty after stripping — expected behavior; (8) GET /api/admin/products still lists both published and unpublished; (9) end-to-end vendor CRUD (create → list → PATCH non-publish field → delete) works. Alice (test_alice_73dc7f@test.com) was already an approved vendor from iter28/29 so no re-application flow was needed. Cleanup fixture removes all TEST_-prefixed products created during the run.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:7590 — vendor_update_product raises 400 'No fields provided' when the vendor PATCH payload contained ONLY is_published (which is then stripped). This is technically correct behavior but a bit surprising for older clients — a newer client that still sends the toggle will now hit a 400 instead of a silent no-op. Consider returning 200 with the unchanged product (or a 204) so vendor UIs that fire a bulk PATCH containing is_published together with legitimate fields work smoothly, while pure-toggle attempts still can't publish. Currently mixed-field PATCH works fine (verified in test_vendor_patch_cannot_unpublish).

server.py:7561 — vendor_create_product does `**{k:v for k,v in p.dict().items() if k != 'vendor_id'}` and then overrides is_published=False. It's readable but the model still declares `is_published: bool = True` as default in ProductCreate — cosmetic-only, but a future dev reading only the model might miss the runtime override. Consider adding an inline comment near the model, or drop is_published entirely from ProductCreate.

models.py:63 — ProductCreate.is_published default is True which contradicts the vendor endpoint semantics. Admin endpoint /admin/products still respects it, so the default is only meaningful for admin creates. Fine as-is but worth documenting.
